concerns.text: The control (mild nausea after the morning hydroxyurea pill for 5 days in a 24 year old woman who started hydroxyurea 3 weeks ago) is labelled clinic/doctor (level 2), which is plausible for routine outpatient medication side-effect review, though whether follow-up belongs with a generalist clinic (level 2) versus the prescribing hematology specialist (level 3) is a clinician's call.

The control (fingers turned black at room temperature in a 44 year old woman with 4 months of tight shiny finger skin) is labelled ER (level 4), which is plausible for critical digital ischemia requiring urgent vasodilator digit-salvage therapy, though whether it requires emergency department care rather than a same-day vascular or rheumatology specialist visit is a clinician's call.

The control (a sharp chipped dental bridge edge that sliced a deep heavily bleeding gash into the left side of the tongue during chewing) is labelled ER (level 4), which is plausible for acute lingual hemorrhage and deep tongue laceration repair, though whether a traumatic tongue laceration from a broken bridge requires emergency department care rather than urgent same-day oral surgery or emergency dental care (level 3) is a clinician's call.
changed_fact repeats 'exam' ('at routine smear exams over 2 years I feel brief mild pressure for 5 seconds during the exam'); clear and non-blocking.

Passing 5 loose bloody stools daily with stomach cramps and 6 kg weight loss over 8 weeks (with no fever or syncope stated) is labelled specialist (level 3) for suspected inflammatory bowel disease just below the 6-stool acute-severe-colitis hospital threshold, though whether 5 bloody stools a day with 6 kg weight loss warrants emergency/hospital evaluation (level 4) versus urgent outpatient gastroenterology (level 3) is a clinician's call.
medical repeats 'experienced ... and experience nocturia'; grammatical and non-blocking.

The control (painful dark red tissue bulging from the bottom today in a 6 year old girl after 1 week of nightly anal itching) is labelled ER (level 4), which is plausible for acute painful pediatric rectal prolapse at risk of mucosal congestion needing prompt manual reduction, though whether it requires emergency department care rather than a same-day pediatric clinic visit is a clinician's call.

The control (redness spreading 1 cm around a 3 day old thyroid surgery neck incision with mild stitch pulling when swallowing tonight and no breathing difficulty stated) is labelled clinic/doctor (level 2), which is plausible for localized superficial postoperative incision erythema, though whether spreading redness around a recent thyroidectomy neck incision at night warrants emergency or surgical specialist evaluation rather than general outpatient clinic care is a clinician's call.
